An accepted assessment becomes advice in three steps: stock status against reference points, a standard advice format, and, where needed, a harvest control rule tested by (simplified) MSE.

```{r}

```

## Comparing management options: FPAT

Where the question is *which measure* (a size limit, an effort cap, a closure or a catch limit) rather than *which catch*, the [Fisheries Performance Assessment Toolkit](fpat.qmd) (FAO Technical Paper 737) provides a participatory route:

::: {.path}
[1 · Benchmark: FPI and governance](../methods/empirical/fpi.qmd){.step} [→]{.arrow} [2 · Plan: FPAT App MSE](fpat.qmd){.step} [→]{.arrow} [3 · Decide]{.step} [→]{.arrow} [4 · Monitor and repeat]{.step}
:::

The benchmarking shows where the fishery underperforms and which measures are feasible to enforce; the FPAT App compares those measures in simulation; the choice is made with stakeholders and re-assessed as data improve. FPAT is the quick screening end of MSE. Harvest control rules for formal adoption are tested with [FLR mse](mse.qmd).
